parts.title: Something Strange
parts.text: It started on a Wednesday when Ravi went to return a book to the library shelf, nearly dropped it, and had to **lunge** to catch it before it hit the floor. Then she noticed something odd. All the other students had gone home — everyone **except** Ravi. A light glowed inside the supposedly locked room. Someone had left a drawing behind — detailed and careful, but strangely **monotonous**, the same tiny symbols repeating row after row, none of them ones she had ever seen before.

parts.title: The Investigation
parts.text: That night a storm vented its **wrath** on the school windows, but Ravi was too curious to sleep. She needed to **locate** where the drawing had come from and copy every detail in sketches before it disappeared, nervously starting to **gnaw** the end of her pencil. She showed it to Nisha, who warned that grown-ups might not like children to **meddle** in old school records, but who helped trace its origins anyway. Together they made real **progress** through the clues. To solve it fully, they needed to **enable** Aisha to join them, unlocking her access to the storage room where old yearbooks were kept.

parts.title: The Hidden Clue
parts.text: Behind the oldest bookshelf, they found a door. Beyond it was a corridor that ran under the school like the underside of a long **pier**, low and damp and echoey, stretching away into darkness. A notice on the wall named a long-forgotten **resident** of the school — a caretaker from 1923 who had been stranded at the school during a great storm, living like a **castaway** for three days until the flood waters receded — and described a box he had sealed and hidden before leaving. "We're going to find something extraordinary," Nisha said, and none of them doubted it.

parts.title: The Secret Revealed
parts.text: What they found was the school's original time capsule from 1923, filled with letters, photographs, and a gold pocket watch. Solving the mystery made all three of them proud. The principal was thrilled and announced that every resident of the school community should come and see it. Their names were added to the school's Hall of Fame, and the time capsule went on permanent display in the library for everyone to admire.

secretPassage.instructions: Read the passage below. Fill in each blank with the correct vocabulary word from the word bank.
secretPassage.passage: The old fisherman stood at the end of the long wooden _(1)_, watching the morning mist lift off the water. He was a lifelong _(2)_ of the harbour village — he had lived there for seventy years and knew every boat, every rock, and every face. He never liked to _(3)_ in other people's affairs, and that discretion made him well known throughout the region: people came from far away just to sit beside him and talk. He told the story of a _(4)_ sailor who had once been stranded alone on a deserted island for six months, with nothing _(5)_ a knife and a waterproof coat to help him survive. That survivor had learned to _(6)_ fresh water by finding plants that collected dew overnight. The sailor's story of courage and endurance told of the sea's terrible _(7)_ — a furious anger that had wrecked a dozen boats in a single night. The fisherman explained that a modern map could _(8)_ even a beginner to steer to any spot in the ocean within metres, a remarkable _(9)_ from the old days when sailors used only stars and guesswork. His old cat would _(10)_ at any silver fish that flopped on the planks, springing forward in a sudden rush. His old dog liked to _(11)_ a bone beside his chair for hours, chewing it down to nothing. The days at sea were long and _(12)_, with the same gray water, the same gray sky, and the same slow hours repeating themselves.
